edits.find: Grouped by owner rather than by which option declared them, so a reader looking for what a compiled Track costs finds three members together instead of five fields spread through a declaration list. See ADR-059, ADR-060, ADR-061, ADR-062 and ADR-067.

Grouped by owner rather than by which option declared them, so a reader looking for what a compiled Track costs finds three members together instead of five fields spread through a declaration list. See ADR-059, ADR-060, ADR-061, ADR-062 and ADR-067.

Two things a port record would otherwise have changed by existing are answered at the resolution rather than left to it, because both are public callback behaviour and this slice moves nothing observable. A hook was a field reached as this.#hook?.(...), so an ordinary method-style host function read this runtime as its receiver, and one reached off a frozen port record would read that record instead; installed() applies each option to this runtime, so the receiver is what it was. And a host that answered a defined non-function answered no completion this layer may discard: complete?.() reached that value and threw a TypeError at the settlement step that ran it, after adoption, so completing() answers the step that call always was and the throw stays where it was thrown. Nothing in this repository relies on either, every hook being an arrow or already bound and every completion a function or nothing, which is exactly why both are stated here rather than discovered from a caller later. See ADR-061 and ADR-071.

edits.find: Beside them, phase A of [#443](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/443) is open in review: `refusal.ts` states the thirteen refusals of the project runtime as one branded union with one describer, one error switch and byte-identical messages, `results.ts` states validation, the live-write seam and handle liveness as three more, and `schema-refusals.ts` keeps its eight names as one call each so no call site moves. Step 3 states that lifecycle as `project-phase.ts`: one branded union over the open scope, the commit depth and whether teardown has begun, with `admit` the one total answer to what each phase admits, pinned against a transcription of the guards it replaces. Step 3b decodes the runtime's validations through `expectValid` and its handle resolutions through `resolveToken` and `expectLive`, so fifteen inline throws, eight retyped diagnostic templates and both stale-handle constructions have one owner each. Step 3c retires all five of `#open`, `#valueSeeds`, `#disposed`, `#inFlight` and `#pendingTeardown` into one `#phase`, so the two guard rungs, `#commit`'s three checks and the clears `#teardown` wrote by hand have one owner too. Step 4 does the same for `TrackEntry`'s `overlay` and `liveWrite`, whose four combinations included one nothing could reach: `value-state.ts` states the three that remain, the emptiness test three members spelled becomes one mint, and the second map write that insured a boolean across a throwing getter is gone with it. Step 5 does it for the last of the wrappers: `authoring-edit.ts` states the eight authored edits a `TrackHandle` asks for as one union applied by one total switch, so two shared orderings, six primitive wrappers, the retained-record write they ended at and the `add: boolean` that decided which of two opposite observation edits was meant are one member. Step 6 of phase A is now open in review: `commit-plan.ts` and `run-plan.ts` make structural commit effects and settlements discriminated data, with pure planning, exhaustive inversion and one impure runner; steps 7 and 8 remain ordered in the pull request body and are not on `main`. Slice narrative, exact-head CI and byte sizes belong to the PRs.
edits.replace: Beside them, phase A of [#443](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/443) is open in review and holds seven of its eight steps: `refusal.ts` and `results.ts` state the project runtime's thirteen refusals and its three decoded results as branded unions with byte-identical messages, `project-phase.ts` states the whole lifecycle as one union over open scope, commit depth and retirement with `admit` the total answer to what each phase admits, `value-state.ts` states what a live write leaves, `authoring-edit.ts` states the eight authored edits one total switch applies, `commit-plan.ts` and `run-plan.ts` make commit effects and settlements pure data with exhaustive inversion and one impure walk, and `project-ports.ts` states every host seam as four total records resolved once at construction. Between them they retire five lifecycle fields, three guard helpers, ten authoring wrappers, fifteen optional hook fields and every `?.` in the runtime body, and no export of `packages/core` moves. What is not done is step 8, the handles, which owes a shared prototype-aware helper first because six test files read a handle's own enumerable keys; the live-write decode is owed beside it. Slice narrative, exact-head CI and byte sizes belong to the PR.
